note: Large area along the One Hundred and Two River northeast of Savannah, with a separate lake tract to the northeast. MDC marks nine primitive camping spots, each beside a small gravel parking lot: six on the river tract, reached from several county roads, and three on the lake tract off Route D and County Roads 182 and 217. None is at the lake itself. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Camping: Individual Campsites', Rule 140 standard; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map'; map (8/2/2021) nine Primitive Camping symbols, each paired with a Parking Lot = GIS 117-125. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights manual. Pin = GIS 118 on lot 83 (river tract), fine. SPLIT PROPOSED: the lake tract (GIS 123-125) is 4.5-6.8 km NE with its own roads. Not waterfront kept. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Individual Campsites'; Rule 140 standard text, no permit rule. Brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map.' Map (last updated 8/2/2021) legend 'Primitive Camping'; nine symbols, each beside a Parking Lot symbol (= GIS 117-125; each within ~35 m of a GIS 26 lot). Imagery of 118, 123, 124, 125: each is a small gravel lot (~20 x 30 m) on or at the end of a gravel lane, with the camping point on the grass beside it. Designated points beside lots - stay. No horse camp, ford or rig wording; roads in are county gravel roads.

SPLIT PROPOSED: the area has two separate tracts on MDC's map. River tract (left panel): camps 117-122, all within ~2 km of the pin, on county roads 186/190/193/194. Lake tract (right panel, around Happy Holler Lake, the 'Lake entrance' on Route D): camps 125 (lot 67, by Route D near Silt Basin 6), 123 (lot 62, end of a lane off the east side, toward Route 198/217) and 124 (lot 63, on County Road 182) - 4.5-6.8 km NE of the pin, on their own roads. Candidate new entry 'Happy Holler Lake Conservation Area (lake tract)' at lot 67 / camp 125, 40.02950,-94.73800 (by the lake entrance road, ~0.7 km from the lake). near.py: nothing else in campgrounds.json within 3 km of 123, 124 or 125. Not waterfront for the split either: 125 has only a small pond ~45 m S (under 5 acres); the lake is ~0.7 km away; 123 and 124 sit in fields.

PIN: stored 39.97466,-94.77501 = GIS 118, 6 m from lot 83, a gravel widening at a bend of the area road on the river tract; no change. No camp on either tract stands out as the main one (all are small lot-side spots). If AWH would rather the existing entry, named for the lake, stand for the lake tract, move it to 40.02950,-94.73800 and the split becomes the river tract (e.g. at GIS 118).
WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): at 118 a small pond lies ~60 m SE through woods; the One Hundred and Two River is several hundred metres away.
PHONE: area page 'For more information call (816) 271-3100' matches stored.
Season (manual, year-round) left as stored. The page lists Waterfowl Hunting / Open Hunting; no closure zones are marked at the camps.
